title: Greenhouse VPD Stress Window
dataSources: Weather-station observations (`ecowitt:obs`, `weatherflow:obs`), air-quality readings (`purpleair:aqi`, `airgradient:sensor`), soil-moisture and greenhouse sensors (`plant:sensor`), aquarium controllers (`aquarium:sensor`).
app: Personal weather stations (Ecowitt/Ambient/Davis/WeatherFlow), air-quality sensors (PurpleAir/AirGradient), and aquarium/greenhouse/soil sensors via HEC and MQTT.
spl:
index=personal sourcetype=plant:sensor
| stats latest(temp_c) as temp_c, latest(humidity_pct) as humidity_pct by zone
| eval vpd_proxy=round((100-humidity_pct)*temp_c/100,2)
| where vpd_proxy>1.6
| sort - vpd_proxy
description: Uses a simple vapor-pressure-deficit proxy to identify greenhouse zones that are too hot and dry for the plants currently living there.
value: Garden sensors are most useful when they become decisions, and VPD is one of the best single signals for plant stress in enclosed growing spaces.
implementation: Forward greenhouse temperature and humidity readings; review zones with elevated VPD proxy and adjust ventilation, shading, or watering.
visualization: Zone table of temperature, humidity, and VPD proxy.
grandmaExplanation: It counts which parts of the greenhouse are feeling too hot and dry for the plants.
